summary: SEC131 deep-reviewed a transactional deploy/rollback design and stopped before executor implementation because repository sources cannot prove the installed Podman Compose 1.3.0 service-only/no-dependency switch and rollback semantics. It adds a no-Go packet and a fixed source-redacted capability observer whose help evidence cannot prove semantics and whose bounded installed-source audit is AST/function scoped. The coherent deferred model binds exact revisions and fresh SEC129 evidence, a single fetch/lock, detached release worktree, revision manifest, app-only switch, health-gated ff-only checkout advance, allowlisted metadata preservation and exactly one post-switch rollback attempt. Root readback rejected the first expanded candidate because its versioned patch remained SEC130-era; the repaired closure requires direct exact-HEAD generation and an independent fresh-alternate-index replay of all 84 paths before the 85th durable patch path is accepted. No live or real-index Git action occurred.

decision.smallest_safe_frontier: The repaired deterministic patch must remain bound to its exact manifest and alternate-index replay evidence. The exact SEC131 expanded stage/commit/push phrase may now be requested but remains ungranted. After publication, the exact capability observation is a separate requestable-not-granted gate. No deploy executor or deploy Go exists.

contract_evidence: Security-incident delivery and notification contracts are dry-run/no-send.
Generic Telegram delivery requires opaque target readiness, the reply gate and an allowed target.
The current agent-safe Debian projection attests TELEGRAM_BOT_TOKEN presence only, not opaque target_configured or TELEGRAM_AGENT_REPLY_ENABLED.
The generic bridge lacks SIRP action-version, single-use grant, expiry, immutable no-retry attempt and independent durable redacted correlation-readback binding.
Activation and runbook contracts require a later exact channel/body/timeout/expiry/no-retry/readback packet.
